rows.title: If storage is too full to set aside a job or project list's unsent changes at sign-out, those changes are lost, and the next sign-in deletes that account's whole list from the cloud
rows.summary: Now: localMeta.write (and memoryMeta.write) returns whether storage took the record. collectionSyncEngine's leave() no longer clears the list while the record holding what was set aside is unsaved. If the first write is refused, the list is cleared first to free room and the record is written again. If that is refused too, the list is put back unchanged, still the account's, and leave() returns false. That account's next sign-in then sends the unsent items and deletes nothing. When another account signs in, its first sync throws a retryable 'resource-exhausted' error (status 'error', retried with backoff). It does not merge the last account's list into the new one. The three tests pin the exact repro (the record cannot grow: list kept, and the next sign-in sends j3 and keeps j1/j2), the room-freeing path (a total quota: the list leaves and j3 is set aside, then sent at the next sign-in) and another account signing in meanwhile.
rows.product_call: When storage cannot hold the set-aside record even after the list is cleared, the signed-out browser keeps showing the account's jobs or projects until the next sign-in. Deleting them would lose data. Another account's first sync waits, retried, until there is room. The owner may want a notice explaining this.
rows.remaining: Product follow-up only: explain to the signed-out user, or to the next account, why the last account list is still shown while storage is too full to set it aside.

rows.title: One job the cloud refuses (an imported id with '/', or a nested array) stops the job sync, and every other job in that batch is held back and called 'too large'
rows.summary: Now: when a first sync's batch of several items is refused for good (failureKind 'stop'), the new commitApart in collectionSyncEngine.js takes it apart, as the résumés' commitHolding does. The deletions and order are sent on their own, then each item on its own. Only an item refused on its own is held; the rest reach the account. When a flush is refused for good with several items, or when its read is refused before anything is sent (an id Firestore cannot name makes fs.doc throw), the batch is no longer held whole or stopped. It is handed to a first sync after the flush pause, and that sync takes it apart. A single refused item is still held as before, and a batch with nothing to hold still stops until the next change. The tests cover an id containing '/' in an imported batch of 20, a nested array in a flush, and a first sign-in on a new browser. In each, only the bad job is held, and the other jobs are written.
rows.product_call: SyncHeldNotice still says a held item is 'too large ... make it smaller' even when the cloud refused it for another reason, such as an id containing '/'. Changing that copy needs a reason carried with each held item. Also, mergeImport/completeJob keep an imported id containing '/', so that job stays on this device only until it is re-created.
rows.remaining: Possible follow-ups, not fixed here: give a reason-specific wording in SyncHeldNotice for a refused, not oversized, item, and have import (jobMerge.js/completeJob) replace ids Firestore cannot use as a document id. Also pre-existing (seen in review): a held item that was restored against the cloud deleted list loses its version in the record the first sync writes, and the next first sync drops it on this browser. Keep the old version for held items that have no cloud doc when writing cloudVersions.

issues: None blocking. Both fixes address the root cause: leave() no longer clears a list whose set-aside record storage refused (the list is cleared first to make room, restored if the record is still refused), and a batch refused for good is taken apart so only the item refused on its own is held. The success path of leave() is unchanged (record written before the list), every caller of meta.write is localMeta/memoryMeta (both now return a boolean), and the stores persist synchronously (setItemWithRoom), so clearing the list really frees room before the second write.

CI checked: failfirst run 36614636156 completed/success; both pairs show "# fail 3" with the src diff reversed, then pass with it. Tests run 36614645842 completed/success at d659e62e. All commits are authored and committed by sairamgudiputi, with no trailers.

Pre-existing, not introduced here (the same on r4-green for an item held as too large): an item restored on this browser after another device deleted it (so it is on the cloud deleted list), and then held, is left out of the record versions written by the first sync. At the next first sync it is neither known nor changed-since, so planFirstSync drops it locally. commitApart only makes held items somewhat more common. Recorded under remaining.

Product note, not fixed: while the last account list cannot be set aside, the signed-out user (or the next account, until its retry succeeds) sees that list and can delete from it. Such deletions are sent to that account at its next sign-in. This is the trade-off the product_call describes.
